name: Largest Strongly Shattered Set
definition: The **Largest Strongly Shattered Set** of $\mathcal{H}$ is the maximum size of a set $S$ for which $\mathcal{H}$ contains an $S$-cube: there is a set $T$ disjoint from $S$ such that $\{T\mathbin{\triangle} A:A\subseteq S\}\subseteq\mathcal{H}$.
graph_summary: The largest dimension of a full subcube contained in the class.
origin_references: Strong shattering and its extremal theory are developed in \cite{bollobas1995defect}.

monotonic.proof: Every cube contained in a subfamily is also a cube contained in the larger class, so the maximum cube dimension cannot decrease when concepts are added.

p_monotonic.proof: Counterexample: $\mathcal H=\{000,011,101,110\}$ has no one-inclusion edge, hence no nonempty contained cube and value 0. Projecting to its first two coordinates gives the full two-cube $\{00,01,10,11\}$, of value 2.

c_monotonic.proof: A cube contained in a conditioned fibre lifts to a cube in the original class by adjoining the fixed labels, so its dimension cannot increase.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, doubly monotonicity requires both subfamily monotonicity and projection monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.

strictly_monotonic.proof: By definition, strictly monotonicity requires both doubly monotonicity and strict c-monotonicity; the recorded failure of one of them rules it out.
